props.title: Detroit

sections.content: **Detroit** (2017) represents Kathryn Bigelow's unflinching examination of the 1967 Detroit riots, specifically the Algiers Motel incident. Like her earlier works **The Hurt Locker** (2008) and **Zero Dark Thirty** (2012), Bigelow employs documentary-style cinematography and intense close-ups to create visceral tension. The film joins other powerful civil rights era chronicles like **Selma** (2014) and **Malcolm X** (1992) in depicting systemic racism and police brutality, though Bigelow's approach feels more like a horror film in its sustained, claustrophobic terror.

sections.content: The film's brutal middle section, taking place almost entirely within the Algiers Motel, draws parallels to other confined-space dramatic thrillers like **12 Angry Men** (1957) and **Dog Day Afternoon** (1975). Will Poulter's chilling performance as racist officer Krauss echoes other portrayals of institutional evil, like Michael Fassbender's Edwin Epps in **12 Years a Slave** (2013) and Ralph Fiennes' Amon Göth in **Schindler's List** (1993).

Bigelow's decision to shoot on digital with cinematographer Barry Ackroyd creates an immediate, documentary feel similar to Paul Greengrass's **Bloody Sunday** (2002) and **United 93** (2006). This technique amplifies the horror of the events while maintaining historical authenticity. The film's structure, beginning with an animated sequence explaining the Great Migration and ending with courtroom drama, mirrors other historical epics like **Mississippi Burning** (1988). sections.content: **Detroit** connects to a broader wave of 21st-century films examining America's civil rights struggles, including **Loving** (2016), **Hidden Figures** (2016), and **The Butler** (2013). These films share a commitment to exposing historical injustices while drawing clear lines to contemporary racial issues. The film's release in 2017, amid heightened awareness of police brutality, makes it particularly resonant with other recent works like **The Hate U Give** (2018) and **Queen & Slim** (2019).
